label: prop:two-vortex-channel-algebra
title: Channel algebra of the two-vortex interaction
html:
Proposition. Channel algebra of the two-vortex interaction

Lean sibling: generic commutative ring, no archimedean input; library module QOU.FluidDynamics.TwoVortexChannelAlgebra.

Proposition (channel algebra of the two-vortex interaction). Let R be a commutative ring carrying elements e_+, e_-, \sigma, q, u satisfying

  \underbrace{e_+ + e_- = 1}_{\text{partition of unity}}, \qquad
  \underbrace{e_+ e_- = 0}_{\text{orthogonality}}, \qquad
  \underbrace{q\,u = 1}_{\text{inverse witness}}, \qquad
  \underbrace{\sigma = q\,e_+ - u\,e_-}_{\text{spectral form}}.

These axioms imply

  \underbrace{e_+^2 = e_+,\ \ e_-^2 = e_-}_{\text{derived idempotency}}; \qquad
  \underbrace{\sigma^2 = q^2\,e_+ + u^2\,e_-}_{\text{spectral square, from partition + orthogonality}}; \qquad
  \underbrace{\sigma^2 = (q - u)\,\sigma + 1}_{\text{Hecke relation}}.

The theorem channel_algebra unites these derivations. The parallel identity (-q^{-1})/q = -(q^2)^{-1} — defining the per-crossing eigenvalue ratio over any field without channel data — resides in the standalone lemma eigenvalue_ratio.

The primary model assigns these elements to the commutant of \sigma_1 in the two-strand Hecke algebra H_2(q). Here e_\pm represents the Wedderburn pair of the Hopf channel and \sigma represents the braid operator of the R-matrix braiding. Setting u = q^{-1} casts the spectral form as the eigenvalue decomposition of \sigma_1 supporting eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}. The resulting Hecke relation proves that the abstract channel data logically forces the Skein relation without external topological presentation.
